title: Book One · Chapter 28: The Coins
story:
Mum opens the folded packet on Jun's table.

Inside is the one coin. Beside it is the note with the date and the words FOR PAPER AND PASTE.

Ronan puts the coin in Jun's hand.

"I couldn't do the kite," he says. "This comes back."

Jun closes his fingers round it. He looks at his mother.

She checks the coin and the note. Then she writes RETURNED across the bottom and puts her name beside it. Mum gives her the note. Ronan keeps a little copy with the same date.

"I wanted the kite more than the coin," Jun says.

"I know."

Jun's mother checks the note. "The money is all back," she says. "Jun may still be upset. He waited for a kite."

Ronan looks at Jun's closed hand. Ronan gave the coin back. He wanted Jun to smile. But Jun is still upset.

On the way home, he asks Mum, "Should I give Jun one of my own coins too?"

"Why?"

"To make it better."

"Which coin did you promise to return?"

"The material coin."

"And you did. You must also tell him sooner next time. Another coin can't do that for you."

At home, Ronan gets the tea box. Three coins lie on his little counting paper. There is a scratch on the blue flower. Ronan did not see it before.

He takes the coins out and puts them beside the copy of the return note.

"Those are different things," Dad says from the door.

"I know. I'm checking."

Dad sits beside him. He has a small bag of smooth bamboo strips. He finished a paid job first. Then he made these strips at home.

"Too late?" he asks.

"For the others. Not for ours."

Dad puts the strips on the board. Ronan tells him about returning the coin. He also tells him about the two unpaid promises. He told those families the truth too. One child doesn't want another kite at all. The girl with the little sister says they may ask again another time, but she isn't asking today.

"So nobody is waiting for Wednesday?" Dad asks.

"Only me and Leo."

"That sounds clearer."

Ronan puts his three coins back. Mum brings out a short length of brown string to tie around the return note. He will keep it in a small pocket inside his school bag until the week is over.

"Can I buy more paper?" he asks.

"Mrs Lan has a rice bag," Mum says. "One side is clean. Ask her first. She may let you use the paper."

"I don't want to owe another kite."

"She isn't asking for one."

Ronan goes to the front room. Mrs Lan is cleaning her glasses. He asks about the bag and waits while she finds it.

"You can have the clean side," she says. "The rice is mine."

He thanks her. He carries the bag back with two hands. He does not let it rub against the wall. This paper is clean and dry.

That evening, he and Leo put it flat on the board. Leo reads the return note once and gives it back without a joke. Then he points to the first kite.

"Can we check the top? Why does it point down?"

Ronan moves the new paper aside. Their first kite lies in front of them. They will not make any new kites tonight. Leo holds one edge. Ronan checks the new line. They can work on this kite together.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：returned＝已归还；copy＝副本；owe＝欠；rice＝米。

理解问题：

1. Jun 的材料钱怎样处理？
2. Ronan 为什么想多给 Jun 一枚自己的硬币？Mum 怎样回答？
